title: Future Foresight Methodologies
overview: Future foresight is a structured approach to exploring how external forces, emerging developments, uncertainties, and strategic choices may shape different possible futures. It does not attempt to predict one certain future. Instead, it helps organizations broaden their field of view, challenge assumptions, anticipate change, recognize emerging opportunities and risks, and make present-day decisions that remain more robust under different future conditions.

This course introduces participants to the principal methodologies used in practical foresight work. Participants will learn how to define a foresight question, establish an appropriate time horizon, scan the external environment, identify trends and weak signals, analyze drivers of change, distinguish predetermined elements from critical uncertainties, build scenarios, explore implications, use backcasting, identify strategic options, and translate foresight findings into planning and decision making.

The program is application-focused. Participants will use structured tools and workshops to move from environmental scanning through scenario development and strategic interpretation, culminating in a practical foresight exercise relevant to an organizational or sectoral challenge.
audience: Senior managers, department heads, strategy and planning professionals, policy personnel, innovation teams, risk and resilience professionals, transformation leaders, project and program managers, researchers, analysts, and employees responsible for long-term planning, strategic decision making, policy development, organizational preparedness, or anticipating emerging opportunities and challenges.
methodology: The course uses an interactive methodology combining short presentations, foresight case studies, horizon-scanning exercises, trend and signal analysis, PESTLE/STEEP analysis, driver mapping, uncertainty assessment, scenario-building workshops, scenario narratives, implication analysis, backcasting, wind-tunneling exercises, group discussions, and strategic action planning. Participants will progressively develop a foresight study around a selected organizational or sectoral issue.
objectivesIntro: By the end of the course, participants will be able to:
objectives: Explain the purpose and limitations of future foresight and distinguish it from forecasting and prediction.
Frame a clear foresight question and select an appropriate time horizon and scope.
Conduct structured environmental and horizon scanning for relevant external developments.
Differentiate trends, emerging issues, weak signals, drivers of change, and uncertainties.
Analyze how political, economic, social, technological, legal, environmental, and other forces may interact.
Identify critical uncertainties that can materially change future conditions.
Develop coherent and sufficiently differentiated future scenarios.
Assess the implications of alternative scenarios for stakeholders, capabilities, risks, opportunities, and strategic priorities.
Apply backcasting and wind-tunneling techniques to improve strategic choices.
Translate foresight insights into practical indicators, options, and actions for present-day planning.
